title: Joint Knowledge Graph Completion and Question Answering

problem.claim: Knowledge graph reasoning includes knowledge graph completion and multi-hop question answering as representative reasoning tasks.

gap.claim: Existing work usually treats knowledge graph completion and multi-hop question answering separately, despite their stated close relationship and potential to benefit from each other.

contributions.claim: The work proposes BiNet, a neural model that jointly handles knowledge graph completion and multi-hop knowledge-graph question answering.
BiNet formulates the joint handling of the two tasks as a multi-task learning problem.
BiNet uses a shared embedding space and an answer scoring module to share latent features and learn interactions between the natural-language question decoder and answer scoring module.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that BiNet addresses both multi-hop knowledge-graph question answering and knowledge graph completion simultaneously with superior performance compared with existing methods.
The authors report that BiNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods across a wide range of knowledge-graph question-answering and knowledge-graph-completion benchmark datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Knowledge graph reasoning supports many real-world applications, and knowledge graph completion and multi-hop question answering are representative tasks.
Most existing work treats the two tasks separately, although the authors view them as closely related and mutually beneficial.
The authors propose BiNet as a multi-task neural model that jointly handles both tasks.
BiNet uses shared embeddings and answer scoring to share latent features and model interactions between question decoding and answer scoring.
The authors report superior performance over existing and state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract describes the two reasoning tasks as closely related and jointly beneficial.

interpretation.claim: Related tasks may provide useful shared representations or complementary learning signals.

application.claim: When designing systems for multiple related knowledge-graph reasoning tasks, consider a shared multi-task formulation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when joint modeling is preferable to separate models or whether the reported benefit generalizes beyond the stated benchmarks.

unknowns: The specific benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, and numerical results are not provided.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training procedure, computational requirements, or ablation results.
The abstract does not independently verify the reported state-of-the-art comparisons.
